transcript: Abolition of nuclear weapons may sound idealistic, but in Japan, which experienced Hiroshima and Nagasaki, this is necessarily an unavoidable theme. Today, there are about 12 500 nuclear warheads in the world. Most are held by the United States and Russia. Their military value is said to lie in being unusable weapons that exercise deterrence. But deterrence may, like a flood, sweep everything away. A wrong judgment, an accident, a seizure by terrorists Once used, the civilized world ends Survivors of the bombs have kept telling the partly remembered stories Burnt skin, radiation, sickness, black rain Things a human must not do to another human In 2017, the treaty on the prohibition of nuclear weapons Was adopted at the UN One twenty-twenty-two countries voted in favor But all nuclear arms states Japan, though the only country to have been bombed, did not join the treaty because of its security policy. This contradiction is a great issue in Japanese society. Most are held by the United States and Russia.

Things a human must not do to another human
In 2017, the treaty on the prohibition of nuclear weapons
Was adopted at the UN
One twenty-twenty-two countries voted in favor
But all nuclear arms states
Japan, though the only country to have been bombed, did not join the treaty because of
its security policy.
This contradiction is a great issue in Japanese society.
Depending on America's nuclear umbrella while calling for abolition
This tension remains the subject of ethical and security debate
